open: Owner suite: resized to about 7 m by 6.5 m. Confirm with the design team.
ADA figures: standard building values, not yet checked against 36 CFR Part 1191.
Door widths, thresholds and turning spaces: not modelled.
Lift car: 1.5 m by 2.0 m internal, to be designed.
Roof level: +9.30 m assumed to match the Bridge floor. Not confirmed on any sheet.
Layout coordinates: read from the schematic, not dimensioned.
Mast positions and aft envelope widths: approximate, read from the sections sheet.
Render 12 shows a wheel as well as touch screens.
Most systems parameters: To be determined.
Guest-facing app scope: not confirmed.
Security hardening: deferred to the testing phase.
Medical bay: no room, equipment list or clinical standard chosen. Not placed on any deck.
Starboard tender service: tender size, weight and launch method not set. Not placed.
Internal tender storage: tender size and count (two) known, but not the stowed dimensions or the fuel and battery arrangements. Not placed.

Mag-rail reload: the passenger lift car (1.5 m by 2.0 m) cannot carry a tender, so reload needs a Tank-level rail and a starboard transfer point. No route through the fuel tank block or to an aft hatch is on the layout.
Tender and bay use conflicts: the bay dinner-for-two depends on tender support, so the bay and the tenders must be planned together.
Pet and animal provision: no standard, species or count chosen. Pet relief area is outdoor and not counted in the hull-plan budget.
Tender EMS fit-out: AED and CPR kit on tenders one and two. Stowage, power and inspection requirements not yet set.

Energy architecture: LFP battery buffer charged by all generation, under a marine-grade EMS and BMS. Battery capacity, cell supplier, EMS product and class/flag requirements not set (docs/energy-management-architecture.md).

Battery room: module size (6 kWh needed for eight racks), 9.6 m² floor on the Tank level, gas-tight exhaust route to a safe outside point, closed-loop cooling load, and pressure-relief sizing from the fire-safety review.
Control software: separate body of work, not started. Public side only keeps the rule that the public build has no route to any vessel control system (docs/control-software-architecture.md).
Exterior: teak or synthetic decking, and the sourcing standard for teak. Stainless or titanium fittings against chrome plating. Docs/exterior-and-maintenance.md.
Spares quantities and stowage for furniture, tableware and soft goods, once service intervals and furniture counts are known.
Maintenance records and crew checklists: native iOS or web app. Public side content only; no control connection.

Materials policy (docs/materials-policy.md): no foam anywhere, teak only outdoors, no synthetic outdoor accommodation. Conflicts to decide: tender hulls, buoyancy, safety equipment, gaskets, sails, rope, medical cases, battery pads, mineral wool.

Materials: silk excluded by the owner. Leather, down, hemp, jute, sisal, cork and regenerated fibres still to decide. Render briefs in IMAGE_GENERATION.json conflict with the policy and need regenerating. Ivory as a material is excluded, including reclaimed ivory (docs/materials-policy.md).
Battery room breather: the proposed membrane vent is usually PTFE (excluded). Replace with a non-PTFE vent (e.g. sintered stainless) and check IP67 and fire review (docs/materials-policy.md).
Exotic materials banned by owner. Open: is teak exotic (affects outdoor decking), and the definition of exotic (docs/materials-policy.md).

Sustainable, non-synthetic materials direction: candidates listed in docs/materials-policy.md. Open: teak status (exotic or certified plantation), leather, outdoor fabric performance, titanium production route.
Silk, gold and silver excluded by owner (docs/materials-policy.md). Confirm this was meant as a ban; recycled precious metal is the only variant that could be reconsidered.
Stainless steel (316 or better, high recycled content) approved for interior and exterior use (docs/materials-policy.md). Chrome plating is not covered by this approval.

Owner rule: stainless steel for all rigid appointments. Conflicts with wood joinery, adds weight (register still 0% covered), and needs galvanic isolation. Decide whether joinery and hull are in scope (docs/materials-policy.md).

Wood: teak only; not structural. Confirm teak is not exotic under the ban (or grant an exception). Decide whether wood joinery is a rigid appointment under the stainless rule (docs/materials-policy.md).

Interior aesthetics deferred. Interior criteria: lightweight and durable. Conflict: the stainless rule for rigid appointments is heavy. Owner to choose which governs the interior (docs/materials-policy.md).
Structural steel for hull, Tank / Technical, Tween and deck. Decide whether synthetic coatings are allowed on structural steel, and whether galvanising is preferred (docs/materials-policy.md).

No steel exposed to the elements. Conflicts: the steel hull in seawater needs a protective system (coating, cathodic protection); teak decking sealant is usually synthetic; does the rule apply to stainless (docs/materials-policy.md).
Sealants allowed as a controlled exception to the no-synthetics rule (finishing and sealing). Approve sealant families, PFAS-free verification and a written procedure (docs/materials-policy.md).

Preservation and maintenance programme documented (docs/preservation-and-maintenance.md). Intervals are placeholders until supplier and class figures exist. Hull protection and coating scope still open.

Painting kit and paint store: store on Tank / Technical separated from fuel and battery, 6 m² placeholder. No paint products approved until the coating decision is made (docs/preservation-and-maintenance.md).

Paint store ventilation: continuous low-level extraction, explosion-proof equipment, dedicated outside exhaust separate from the battery room, and vapour detection with interlock (docs/preservation-and-maintenance.md). Standard and air-change figure to be set by fire-safety review.

Whole-craft ventilation: 13 of 16 outlets have no set position. Separation cannot be proven until the general arrangement is dimensioned (docs/ventilation-strategy.md). Tank level has limited room for separate routes.

Exhaust heat recovery: direct heat use first (battery heating, hot water, water-making); electricity recovery (ORC) is about 4% of load at 20 kW and not worth the weight yet (docs/ventilation-strategy.md).

Genset exhaust and all exhaust needs: pilot house roof outlet not accepted (occupied outdoor helm and guest roof); alternative stern or side stack to be placed. Genset safety permissives, run protections, fuel shut-off and spares documented (docs/genset-exhaust-and-systems.md).

Water supply: atmospheric units sized to drinking water only (5 to 13 units normal, 36 on event days). Reverse osmosis carries all other water. Occupancy and drinking-water figures await owner confirmation (docs/water-supply-scaling.md).

Roll control: gyro stabiliser sized at 1.15e6 kg·m²/s for 231 kN·m peak (ζ 0.10). Genset mounts 27 mm deflection at 90% isolation. Technology choice (gyro or fins) depends on use profile (docs/roll-control-gyro.md).
Toyota EV powerplant is energy production only, feeding the 600 V output bus. Rating, converter efficiency, AC or DC bus choice and marine rating open (docs/hybrid-energy-production.md).

Multiple powerplants on one exhaust: separate outlet per engine preferred; shared manifold only with isolation and non-return valves, back-pressure checks for every combination, and branch drains (docs/genset-exhaust-and-systems.md).

Bus voltage: Toyota EV platform native pack is about 355 V nominal (secondary sources, to verify). Aligning the 600 V bus needs a choice between a full 355 V bus, a DC-DC step-up to a 600 V propulsion bus, or a two-voltage design. Propulsion power decides (docs/bus-voltage-alignment.md).

800 V bus basis: nominal 800 V, window 720 to 880 V, headroom H 1.25 on continuous current at minimum voltage, insulation at least 1,100 V. Propulsion power still needed to size cable (docs/bus-800v-design.md).
Embarked water: buffer only, since water is produced onboard. Outage period for the buffer and drinking-only versus full-demand coverage to decide (docs/water-supply-scaling.md; 72 h placeholder).

Provisioning: frozen store refrigeration (envelope about 0.20 kW average at placeholder U and COP, pull-down unknown) and non-foam walk-in insulation. Food rate and period to confirm (docs/provisioning-food-storage.md).

Provisioning revised: protein fresh from the sea (chill room for daily catch), produce from port held for a placeholder 14-day passage, chilled produce store 4 m². Passage lengths between ports and catch assumption to confirm (docs/provisioning-food-storage.md).

Specialty provisions: wine cellar (4 m², 12 to 14 °C, low vibration), chilled cheese zone (2 m², 2 to 6 °C), frozen butter in the frozen store. Per-person rates are placeholders; wine hold period to confirm (docs/provisioning-food-storage.md).

Dry stores: rice, grains, flour and baking sized at about 0.54 m² floor at placeholder rates (0.15 and 0.05 kg per person per day, 90 days), within the 8 m² dry store. Rates and flour shelf life to confirm (docs/provisioning-food-storage.md).
